sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Hazel Tic Tac Toe is a game of logic and strategy, where players compete against the computer in a battle of wits. The game is played on a 3x3 grid, with players taking turns to place their symbols, either X or O. The objective is to secure three consecutive wins in a row, either horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. But that's not all - the game also features a scoring system, where players earn points for each win, and the game ends when either player reaches a predetermined score.

One of the key features of Hazel Tic Tac Toe is its simplicity. The game is incredibly easy to pick up, with intuitive controls that can be navigated using the mouse. This makes it an excellent choice for kids and adults alike, providing hours of entertainment and mental stimulation. But don't be fooled - the game is also surprisingly challenging, requiring players to think strategically and make tactical decisions to outsmart the computer.

In terms of gameplay mechanics, Hazel Tic Tac Toe is a classic example of a game of perfect information, where both players have complete knowledge of the game state. This means that players can plan their moves carefully, thinking several steps ahead to outmaneuver their opponent. But the game also features a element of unpredictability, as the computer can make unexpected moves, forcing players to adapt and respond accordingly.
